description.translation: Choose which service translates Arabic into English while people type. A service is switched on only after it passes a test with its saved data.
description.email: Choose how the platform sends e-mail (sign-in links, invitations, notices). A service is switched on only after it passes a test with its saved data.
description.settings: Translation, e-mail services, and the wording of e-mails and notifications, in one page.
description.captcha: Cloudflare Turnstile check on the e-mail sign-in page. With no service switched on no check is asked. A service is switched on only after it passes a test with its keys.
description.ai: The AI service that places the parts of an uploaded job-title file when the fixed reader cannot read it (the text of the file is sent to the service). A service is switched on only after it passes a test with its key.

serverSettings.email: No service is switched on here, so the e-mail settings on the server are used.
serverSettings.captcha: No service is switched on, so no check is asked at sign-in.
serverSettings.ai: No service is switched on, so the «Analyse with AI» button is not offered.

secretSaved: A value is saved. Leave it blank to keep it, or type a new one.

description.email: Send a short message to any address with the data in the form.

test.problem: The service answered with a problem
test.toHint: Any e-mail address you can open.

test.captchaNeedsForm: Save the site key first, or type it in the form, then try again.

smtp.secure: Turn on for port 465; port 587 upgrades the connection by itself.

ses.from: An address or domain verified in Amazon SES.
ses.region: The region where the sender is verified.

sendgrid.apiKey: Needs the Mail Send permission only.

graph.sender: The mailbox the app sends as. The app needs the Mail.Send application permission.

google.serviceAccountJson: Paste the whole file downloaded from Google Cloud. The account needs the Cloud Translation API User role.

aws.secretAccessKey: Use an IAM user limited to translate:TranslateText.

azure.region: The region of the Translator resource, as shown with its keys.

turnstile.siteKey: Cloudflare dashboard → Turnstile → your widget → «Site key». A public key shown on the sign-in page.
turnstile.secretKey: From the same widget → «Secret key». It is not shown after saving, and must belong to the widget that owns the site key.

anthropic.apiKey: Starts with sk-ant-. Created in the Anthropic console and shown only once.
anthropic.model: A model name: claude-opus-5-5 (the most accurate) or claude-sonnet-5-5 (cheaper). Leave it as is if unsure.

compatible.apiKey: The key of that service. For the free Gemini option: «Get API key» in Google AI Studio.
compatible.baseUrl: A public https address that ends before «/chat/completions». Gemini: https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai · Groq: https://api.groq.com/openai/v1 · OpenRouter: https://openrouter.ai/api/v1
compatible.model: A model of that service that supports structured JSON answers. Free Gemini: gemini-3.8-flash.

noTabs: You may not view any of these settings.

help.title: {{name}}: how to get the data
help.warn: Keep keys secret. Anyone holding them can use the service on your account.

aws.summary: Amazon's translation service. Needs an IAM user's access keys.
steps: Sign in to the AWS Console and open IAM → Users → Create user (for example arweqah-translate).
Attach a policy that allows only translate:TranslateText.
Open the user → Security credentials → Create access key → «Application running outside AWS».
Copy the Access key ID and the Secret access key at once: the secret is shown only one time.
Pick a region where Amazon Translate is available (for example us-east-1 or eu-west-1).

fields.accessKeyId: The public half of the key pair; it looks like AKIA… .
fields.secretAccessKey: The private half, shown once when the key is created. Create a new key if it is lost.
fields.region: The AWS region that receives the translation requests.

google.summary: Google's translation service. Needs a service account key file (JSON).
steps: Open Google Cloud Console, pick or create a project, and make sure billing is on.
Open APIs & Services → Library, search «Cloud Translation API» and press Enable.
Open IAM & Admin → Service Accounts → Create service account.
Give it the role «Cloud Translation API User».
Open the account → Keys → Add key → Create new key → JSON. A file downloads.
Open the file in a text editor and paste all of it here.

fields.serviceAccountJson: The whole JSON file of the service account. It holds the account's e-mail and private key, so it is stored encrypted and never shown again.

azure.summary: Microsoft's translation service (Azure AI Translator). Needs a Translator resource key.
steps: Sign in to the Azure portal → Create a resource → search «Translator» → Create.
Choose a subscription, resource group, region and pricing tier (F0 is free with a monthly limit).
When it is ready open the resource → Keys and Endpoint.
Copy Key 1 and the Location/Region.
Leave the endpoint as it is unless Microsoft gave you a private one.

fields.key: Key 1 or Key 2 of the resource; either one works.
fields.region: The Location/Region shown next to the keys (for example westeurope). A global resource may use «global».
fields.endpoint: The address requests are sent to. The default https://api.cognitive.microsofttranslator.com fits most resources.

smtp.summary: Any mail server that accepts SMTP, such as your hosting or Microsoft 365.
steps: Ask the mail provider (or find in its help) for the SMTP server, port, and whether it needs a user name and password.
Create a mailbox for the platform (for example no-reply@yourdomain) and, if the provider needs it, an app password.
Port 587 uses STARTTLS; port 465 uses TLS and needs «Secure connection» turned on.
Microsoft 365: server smtp.office365.com, port 587, and SMTP AUTH must be enabled for the mailbox.
Use the sender address the server allows this mailbox to send as.

fields.host: The mail server's address, for example smtp.office365.com.
fields.secure: Turn on for port 465. Leave off for 587, which upgrades the connection by itself.
fields.user: The mailbox login, often the full e-mail address. Leave empty for a server that needs none.
fields.password: The mailbox password or app password.
fields.from: What recipients see as the sender, as an address or «Name <address>». The server must allow it.

ses.summary: Amazon's e-mail sending service, through its API.
steps: Open Amazon SES in the AWS Console, in the region you will use.
Verified identities → Create identity: verify your domain (recommended) or one address.
New accounts are in the sandbox (only verified recipients): request production access when ready.
In IAM create a user allowed ses:SendEmail only, then create an access key for it.
Copy the Access key ID and the Secret access key at once; the secret is shown one time.

fields.accessKeyId: The public half of the IAM user's key pair.
fields.secretAccessKey: The private half, shown once when the key is created.
fields.region: The SES region where the sender is verified.
fields.from: The verified address, or any address of the verified domain, as an address or «Name <address>».

sendgrid.summary: SendGrid's e-mail sending service, through its API.
steps: Sign in to SendGrid → Settings → API Keys → Create API Key.
Choose «Restricted Access» and turn on Mail Send only.
Copy the key at once: it is shown one time.
Settings → Sender Authentication: verify a domain or a single sender address.
Use that verified address as the sender here.

fields.apiKey: The key you created; it starts with SG. and needs the Mail Send permission only.
fields.from: A sender verified in SendGrid, as an address or «Name <address>».

graph.summary: Send as a Microsoft 365 mailbox with an app registered in your Entra tenant.
steps: Open the Microsoft Entra admin center → App registrations → New registration.
On the app's Overview copy the Application (client) ID and the Directory (tenant) ID.
Certificates & secrets → New client secret → copy the secret Value at once (not the Secret ID).
API permissions → Add → Microsoft Graph → Application permissions → Mail.Send → Grant admin consent.
Use a real mailbox of your tenant as the sender (a shared mailbox works). Ask IT to limit the app to that mailbox if possible.

fields.tenantId: The Directory (tenant) ID of your Microsoft Entra tenant.
fields.clientId: The Application (client) ID of the registered app.
fields.clientSecret: The secret Value created under Certificates & secrets; it expires on the date you chose, so renew it before then.
fields.sender: The mailbox the app sends as. The app needs the Mail.Send application permission.

turnstile.summary: Cloudflare's free check that tells a person from a bot, without annoying puzzles.
steps: Open the Cloudflare dashboard → Turnstile → Add widget.
Name the widget, add the platform address under «Hostname», and choose the «Managed» mode.
Copy the «Site key» and the «Secret key» once the widget is created.
Paste both here, press «Try», and solve the check in the window.
When the test passes, press «Activate».

fields.siteKey: A public key shown on the sign-in page; it usually starts with 0x4.
fields.secretKey: A secret key that stays on the server and is never shown after saving.

anthropic.summary: Claude, by Anthropic, reads a title file in any order and puts each part in its place. You pay Anthropic by use; reading one title file usually costs well under one dollar.
steps: Open console.anthropic.com and sign in (or create an account for the organisation).
Under Billing, add a payment method and a small credit.
Open Settings → API keys → Create key and name it «Arweqah platform».
Copy the key at once (it is shown only once) and paste it into «API key» here.
Leave the model as it is, or type another model name from the console.
Press «Try». When the test passes, press «Activate».

fields.apiKey: The secret key from the console. It stays on the server and is never shown after saving.
fields.model: The model that reads the files. The default is the most accurate; a cheaper one may miss details.

anthropic.note: The text of every title file analysed with AI is sent to Anthropic. It holds company data, not employees' data: do not paste personal data into it.

compatible.summary: Any service that speaks the OpenAI protocol, so you can use a free one (Google Gemini's free tier needs no card) and keep Claude as the other option. Only one AI service is switched on at a time.
steps: Open aistudio.google.com and sign in with a Google account.
Choose «Get API key» then «Create API key» and copy the key.
Paste it into «API key» here. Leave the address and the model as they are to use the free Gemini.
For another service (Groq, OpenRouter…) type its address and a model it offers that supports structured JSON answers.
Press «Try». When the test passes, press «Activate».

fields.apiKey: The secret key of the service. It stays on the server and is never shown after saving.
fields.baseUrl: Where the service answers: the platform adds «/chat/completions» to it. It must be a public https address.
fields.model: The model that reads the files. Free models are less exact than Claude and have rate limits.

compatible.note: Google's free tier may use what you send to improve its products, and other free services have their own terms. A title file holds company data, not employees' data: do not put personal data in it. The AI's reading is always reviewed by a person before it is saved.
